deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is the opening page of an official administrative report (Gutachten) addressed to the Royal Hanoverian University Curatorium (Königliches Universitäts-Curatorium) in Göttingen.

The heading reads: 'Most obedient report of the provisional Direction of the Royal Observatory and of Professors Riemann and Schering, concerning the undertaking of a Central-European arc measurement (Mittel-Europäische Gradmessung).'

The text records the following. By a rescript of 30 July of the current year, the Curatorium informed the signatories of a request from the Prussian government. Prussia had asked for the cooperation of the Hanoverian government in a project proposed by the Prussian General (z. D., i.e. on standby) Johann Jacob Baeyer. Baeyer's aim, quoted on the page, was 'by connecting the geodetic measurements in those European countries which lie with Germany between the same meridians, to bring into being a Central-European arc measurement.' The Curatorium enclosed Baeyer's memorandum 'Über die Größe und Figur der Erde' (On the size and figure of the Earth). The sentence continues onto the next page, where it becomes clear that the Curatorium requested an expert report on the plan.

Context (mine): Baeyer's memorandum dates from 1861, and the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung was founded in 1862 (later the Europäische and then the Internationale Erdmessung, a forerunner of the IAG). The rescript is therefore almost certainly of 30 July 1861, and the report dates from autumn 1861. After Gauss's death in 1855 the Göttingen observatory was under provisional direction. Riemann and Ernst Schering (Gauss's editor, later involved in geodesy) were consulted as mathematicians. The page serves only to set up the report; any scientific assessment of the geodetic plan would come on later folios.

results.what: Riemann named, together with Schering and the provisional observatory directorate, as co-author of the Göttingen expert report on Baeyer's proposal for a Central-European arc measurement (c. 1861).
results.modern_name: Founding of the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (precursor of the International Association of Geodesy)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely administrative: no mathematics appears. Riemann's participation in a Göttingen faculty report on Baeyer's geodetic project is a minor biographical detail. It fits his position as a Göttingen professor and Gauss's successor in mathematics, but it is not widely discussed. It is only mildly interesting as documentation of his involvement in geodetic policy.
